fields.title: A merge waits for the validate job
fields.evidence: The `validate` check on the pull request, and the branch rule on `main` in the repository settings.

sections.What it checks:
* [std-CI.the-gate-runs-on-every-pull-request-into-main](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/7912e0bf3bf4296cc127ccd8a8fb0d558179fbae/examples/dog-fooding/standards/workflows.md#the-gate-runs-on-every-pull-request-into-main) says the branch rule on `main` "**MUST** name `validate` as
  the check a merge waits for".
* `eng:std-GATES.a-failing-check-stops-the-change` says branch policy "**MUST** block a merge while any required check
  is failing".
sections.How it works:
`kac.yml` declares a `validate` job whose `needs:` lists `corpora`, `tool`, `lint`, `docs`, `round-trip` and `import-round-trip`. The branch rule requires that one check name. The job runs after the others whatever they report, because its `if:` is `always()`. Its one step reads each job's result and fails unless every one is `success`.

Without `always()`, a failed job would skip `validate`. GitHub counts a skipped required check as passing, so the merge would not wait.

Three of those jobs are matrices. A matrix job reports one check per cell: `corpora` reports as `corpora (library)` and three more. A branch rule naming the matrix would wait for a check that never arrives.
sections.Coverage and gaps: The branch rule lives in GitHub's repository settings, and no file in this repository has a copy of it. Nothing in CI reads it, so a rule renamed, relaxed or turned off shows nowhere on the pull request. [ctl-0002](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/7912e0bf3bf4296cc127ccd8a8fb0d558179fbae/examples/dog-fooding/controls/0002-workflow-gate-tests.md) checks the other half: whether `validate` still needs every job.
